now_building.title: Build a CHIP-8 emulator in C++
now_building.summary: A whole computer in about 1,000 lines: memory, a CPU, a screen and a keyboard. Each episode adds one part and answers one question.
now_building.hero_caption: Fig. 1: a CHIP-8 computer, front view. We build one in C++ in the series below.

episodes.title: How do zeros and ones actually run a program?
How does computer memory actually work?
How did old games draw pixels? The XOR trick
How does a computer read keys, keep time and roll dice?
How does a CPU actually work? Fetch, decode, execute

builds.what: A tiny operating system that boots

projects.name: CHIP-8 emulator in C++
projects.text: A CHIP-8 emulator written test-first in modern C++, built one part per episode: memory, the CPU loop, the screen, the keypad and the timers.

projects.name: CS Map
projects.text: A beginner-friendly map of computer science: short topic pages, learning paths and cross-linked concepts, from hardware and operating systems to networks, databases and security.

projects.name: Logichess
projects.status: Coming soon, free and open source
projects.text: A chess tutor that explains why a move is good or bad in terms of what happens on the board. Stockfish finds the moves, a rule-based layer pulls out the reasons, and a language model writes the explanation from that evidence only.
